newSounds: Nasal vowels: ão = nasal 'own' (coração = koh-rah-SOWN), ã = nasal 'ahn' (manhã = mah-NYAHN), -m/-n in the coda nasalises the vowel (bom = BOHN). nh = ny (Telugu ఞ), lh = ly in million, ch = sh, j and g before e/i = zh in measure, ç and c before e/i = s, rr and word-initial r are a throaty h in Brazil while a single r is a tap like Telugu ర.
rhythm: Brazilian Portuguese is largely syllable-timed, close to Telugu: give each vowel its time and do not reduce unstressed vowels the way English does. European Portuguese is stress-timed and swallows weak vowels; the Brazilian rhythm is still understood there.
registerFirst: Start with você plus a third-person verb (você fala, você pode, você gostaria) — the polite everyday register in Brazil; locals move to tu once they know you. Obrigado for a man, obrigada for a woman; in Portugal o senhor / a senhora is the safest formal address.
trap: The big trap is nasality: in coração and manhã the air leaves through the nose with the mouth open — do not tack a hard English -n on the end. The written letter 'h' is silent (hoje = OH-zhee).
